newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS TUESDAY FIRMER ON UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS TUESDAY FIRMER ON UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed on Tuesday stronger against hard currencies, buoyed by a surprise injection of foreign currency into the market by the central Reserve Bank, dealers said.
"The Reserve Bank came in and sold some money at the 10.2400 level... no-one is quite sure why," one dealer commented.
The dealers added however that the local unit had not benefitted from a U.S.$26 million export receipt they had anticipated in the morning.
"If it did come into the market, then whoever got it did not sell the money," said one.
They reiterated that the foreign exchange market had largely ignored an ongoing stand-off between government and civil servants who went on strike over two weeks ago demanding wage rises.

They said the outcome of a cabinet meeting on Tuesday to discuss the fate of those employees dismissed for ignoring a call to go back to work was also unlikely to have much impact on the market, which was largely driven by supply and demand.
At Tuesday's close, the local dollar was trading firmer at 10.2200/3000 against the U.S unit compared to late Monday's 10.2500/3500 and was at 15.9700/16.1320 from 16.0000/1700 versus sterling.
It edged up to 6.8760/9450 from 6.9100/9800 on the mark and to 2.2770/3010 against the rand from 2.2900/3150 the previous day.
